steps.title: Create the app on the project platform
steps.detail: Create a HubSpot app on the project based platform, using the HubSpot CLI and app-hsmeta.json if your account uses that flow. Do not rely on a legacy Create app button that may no longer be there.
steps.blockerTip: HubSpot retired the legacy public app creation UI. If you cannot find the old button, use the project flow.

steps.title: Set redirect URLs and scopes in the app file
steps.detail: Set auth redirectUrls and requiredScopes in the app file, minimum only, for example contacts or crm.objects.contacts.read for the feature you need. Upload the project to apply the change.
steps.blockerTip: Changing redirect URLs in the portal alone may not apply. Update the app file and upload it.

steps.title: Get the client ID and secret from Auth
steps.detail: On the app project details page, open the app, go to Auth, and copy Client ID and Client secret. Store the secret server side.
steps.blockerTip: Never put the secret in client code or a public repo.

steps.title: Send the user to the authorize URL
steps.detail: Send the user to https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope, and redirect_uri. The user picks an account and grants scopes. After approval, HubSpot redirects back with a code.
steps.blockerTip: Optional scopes can be dropped for accounts that do not have that tool. Check granted scopes after install.

steps.title: Exchange the code and test one call
steps.detail: Exchange the code at the token endpoint with grant_type authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, and redirect_uri. Store access and refresh tokens server side, then test one API call.
steps.blockerTip: Access tokens are short lived, about 30 minutes in HubSpot docs summaries. Use the refresh token, do not re-authorize on every call.

tested: Official HubSpot OAuth docs checked on 2026-10-31 via search results. No HubSpot sign-in, app creation, or OAuth test was completed for this guide.
